title: Touring with Bee Palmer and the naming of the New Orleans Rhythm Kings
summary: He left Dixieland for vaudeville and went to Chicago with Bee Palmer, Roppolo, Emmett Hardy and Johnny Frisco; her band name gave the Rhythm Kings theirs.

bands.name: Bee Palmer and her New Orleans Rhythm Kings

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: And we used to play the Italian all the time. But I didn't stay too long with the Italian band, because I started playing with these Dixieland bands. And then when I quit playing with the Dixieland, I went to play vaudeville. And then I went to Chicago with this B. Palmer, the shimmy shaker that came from Chicago. She took Rapport, Emmett Hardy, you know those boys. Frisco, Johnny Frisco. And we played vaudeville. And in fact, that's where the New Orleans Rhythm Kings started. She named, that's what she named the band, B. Palmer and her New Orleans Rhythm Kings.
That's how they got their name?
That's how they got their name?
And so they took their name from her, you see?
Yeah. And she already had Rapp and Emmett Hardy?
Hardy, myself and Frisco. Her husband was the piano player, Al Segal. And that's all in five pieces.
From here. He just died about a couple of years ago. I never knew him. I never knew him. Well, he played with Johnny Long with the Shillen Band for all time. He was raised for a damn good drummer.
